content.description: A UI/UX Designer shapes both the look (UI — layout, visual hierarchy, color, typography) and the feel (UX — flows, interactions, usability) of a digital product, working from user research through wireframes, prototypes, and polished mockups in tools like Figma. They validate design decisions with usability testing and iterate based on user feedback and data before handing off specs to developers. Unlike a Frontend Developer, who writes the production code that renders the interface in a browser, a UI/UX Designer works in design tools and owns the pre-code experience. Unlike a Graphic Designer, who focuses on static visual/brand assets such as logos and marketing collateral, a UI/UX Designer focuses on interactive product flows, information architecture, and usability across a whole user journey.

vnMarket.value: UI/UX Design hiện là một trong những mảng có mức thu nhập tốt nhất trong ngành thiết kế tại Việt Nam, với cơ hội việc làm đa dạng từ startup đến các doanh nghiệp lớn trong và ngoài nước; nhà tuyển dụng ngày càng chú trọng không chỉ kỹ năng thiết kế giao diện mà còn khả năng nghiên cứu hành vi người dùng (UX research) khi tuyển vị trí này.

salary.value: Theo cấp bậc tại Việt Nam: mới ra trường khoảng 10-15 triệu VNĐ/tháng; Junior (0-2 năm) khoảng 12-18 triệu; Senior (4-7 năm, thành thạo Figma, prototyping, UX Research) khoảng 30-45 triệu; các vị trí lâu năm/Lead có thể đạt 45-70+ triệu VNĐ/tháng, với UX Lead tại các công ty công nghệ lớn (VNG, FPT Software, Tiki, MoMo) đạt khoảng 40-55 triệu VNĐ/tháng.

demand.value: VietnamWorks hiện có hơn 800 việc làm UX UI Design đang tuyển (ghi nhận 813 vị trí tại thời điểm truy cập 17/09/2026), cho thấy nhu cầu tuyển dụng vị trí này tại Việt Nam vẫn ở mức cao và tiếp tục tăng.

similarJobs.name: Product Designer
similarJobs.distinction: Carries broader ownership of end-to-end product strategy and UX outcomes, versus a UI/UX Designer's more execution-focused interface and flow design work.

similarJobs.name: Graphic Designer
similarJobs.distinction: Focuses on static visual/brand assets (logos, marketing collateral, print) rather than interactive product flows and usability.

similarJobs.name: Frontend Developer
similarJobs.distinction: Implements the visual design in production code rather than producing the wireframes, mockups, and prototypes themselves.

similarJobs.name: UX Researcher
similarJobs.distinction: Specializes in user research methods (interviews, usability testing, surveys) rather than producing the visual and interaction design deliverables directly.

hardSkills.name: Wireframing & prototyping (Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch)
hardSkills.description: The core toolset for turning ideas into testable low- and high-fidelity representations of a product before any code is written.

hardSkills.name: User research & usability testing
hardSkills.description: Running interviews, surveys, and usability tests (e.g. with Maze, UserTesting, Miro) to validate that a design actually solves the user's problem.

hardSkills.name: Visual design & design systems
hardSkills.description: Applying typography, color, layout, and a consistent component library so the product looks and behaves coherently at scale.

hardSkills.name: Information architecture & user flow mapping
hardSkills.description: Structuring content and navigation so users can find what they need with minimal friction.

hardSkills.name: Basic HTML/CSS for developer handoff
hardSkills.description: Understanding what is technically feasible and communicating design intent precisely to the engineers who will build it.

hardSkills.name: Accessibility standards (WCAG)
hardSkills.description: Designing interfaces usable by people with disabilities is an increasingly explicit requirement from employers and clients.

softSkills.name: User empathy
softSkills.description: Designing from the user's actual context and pain points rather than personal aesthetic preference is central to good UX.

softSkills.name: Creative problem-solving
softSkills.description: Translating a business or user problem into a workable, elegant interface solution, often under tight constraints.

softSkills.name: Cross-functional collaboration
softSkills.description: Working closely with Product Managers, developers, and stakeholders throughout the design and handoff process.

softSkills.name: Presentation & storytelling
softSkills.description: Defending design decisions with a clear rationale in design reviews and stakeholder presentations.

softSkills.name: Adaptability to feedback
softSkills.description: Iterating quickly on designs based on user testing results, stakeholder feedback, and changing requirements.

futureSkills.name: Human-centered design practice (ISO 9241-210)
futureSkills.label: important
futureSkills.description: Thiết kế lấy người dùng làm trung tâm theo chuẩn ISO 9241-210, đảm bảo sản phẩm thực sự giải quyết đúng nhu cầu.

futureSkills.name: Accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1)
futureSkills.label: important
futureSkills.description: Đảm bảo sản phẩm dùng được cho người khuyết tật — ngày càng là yêu cầu bắt buộc ở nhiều thị trường.

futureSkills.name: Data-driven design decision-making
futureSkills.label: important
futureSkills.description: Dùng dữ liệu hành vi người dùng để ra quyết định thiết kế thay vì chỉ dựa vào cảm tính.

futureSkills.name: AI-assisted design & prototyping tools
futureSkills.label: critical
futureSkills.description: Dùng công cụ AI hỗ trợ thiết kế và tạo prototype nhanh hơn, dành thời gian cho tư duy chiến lược sản phẩm.

keySkills: Collaborating directly with developers on handoff
End-to-end UX ownership for a product area
